## Example

Let $T_{2,3}$ be the right-handed trefoil and $-T_{2,3}$ its reverse mirror. A filtered basis for $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(T_{2,3})$ is $x_0,x_1,x_2$ with $(M,A)(x_0)=(0,1)$, $(M,A)(x_1)=(-1,0)$, $(M,A)(x_2)=(-2,-1)$ and differential $\partial x_1=Ux_0+x_2$, $\partial x_0=\partial x_2=0$. Under the conventions of this page,
$$ \epsilon(T_{2,3})=1,\qquad \Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)=\begin{cases}-t,&0\le t\le1,\\ t-2,&1\le t\le2.\end{cases} $$
The graph has its unique interior breakpoint at $t=1$. For the reverse mirror, $\epsilon(-T_{2,3})=-1$ and $\Upsilon_{-T_{2,3}}(t)=-\Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The displayed staircase complex, the epsilon map convention, and the Upsilon cycle-minimax definition.

[F1] [[def-epsilon-from-filtered-knot-floer-complex]]: at $s=\tau$, epsilon is $1$ when $F_s=0$, $-1$ when $G_s=0$, and $0$ when both homology maps are nonzero. These are tests on the exact hook maps, not on an arbitrary representative of the vertical class.

[F2] [[def-upsilon-function-from-filtered-complex]]: $\Upsilon=-2\nu_t$, where $\nu_t$ is the minimum $F_t$-level of a Maslov-zero cycle representing the normalized generator.

[F4] [[lem-epsilon-stable-equivalence-and-not-a-homomorphism]] steps 1.4 and 6.2 give a finite signed-code admission of the positive trefoil grid and compute its normalized three-generator staircase. [[thm-grid-homology-independent-of-grid-and-equals-knot-floer]] supplies the stated normalized grid-to-analytic comparison; its current Proof includes the absolute Maslov and Alexander normalizations and has its [F1]–[F5] prerequisites recorded there.

[F3] [[lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap]]: the reverse-mirror complex is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual, which negates the two filtration coordinates; the actual analytic diagram identification and its absolute grading are supplied without requiring admission of this particular staircase.

[F5] [[thm-grid-upsilon-equals-oss-upsilon]] now has a proof of the grid Upsilon comparison, using the normalized comparison in [F4] and the locally supplied t-modification and tower splitting. Its precise analytic prerequisites are those recorded by [F4].

## Proof

1.1 In the vertical complex, the differential is $x_1\mapsto x_2$, so its degree-zero homology generator is $x_0$ and first appears at Alexander level $1$. The normalized comparison in [F4], after quotient by the chosen $U$ action, identifies this filtered hat complex with the specified-data complex in [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]]; hence $\tau(T_{2,3})=1$. For the exact epsilon maps at $s=1$, the target of $F_1$ contains $U^{-1}x_1$ with boundary $x_0$: its other differential term $U^{-1}x_2$ has $j<1$ and is killed there. Thus $F_1=0$. The source of $G_1$ contains the degree-zero cycle $x_0$, while $U^{-1}x_1$ has $i>0$ and is excluded, so that class survives and maps to the nonzero vertical class. Thus $G_1\ne0$ and the exact three-case definition gives epsilon $1$ for this complex. [given, F1, F4]

1.2 A Maslov-zero cycle representing the normalized total generator is either $x_0$ or $U^{-1}x_2$: the Maslov-zero chain group in the displayed basis is spanned by these two cycles, and $\partial(U^{-1}x_1)=x_0+U^{-1}x_2$ makes their homology classes equal. Their coordinates are $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$, so their filtration levels are $t/2$ and $1-t/2$. Therefore $\nu_t=\min(t/2,1-t/2)$ and $\Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)=-2\nu_t$, which gives the stated two linear pieces. They agree at $t=1$, where the slope changes. [given, F2, algebra]

2.1 The algebraic Laurent dual of the displayed complex has generators $x_0^*,x_1^*,x_2^*$ at Maslov/Alexander values $(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1)$ and differential $\partial x_0^*=Ux_1^*$, $\partial x_2^*=x_1^*$, $\partial x_1^*=0$. In its vertical complex $x_2^*$ maps to $x_1^*$, leaving $x_0^*$ as generator at Alexander level $-1$. At $s=-1$, the $F_{-1}$ target kills $Ux_1^*$ because $i<0$, so $x_0^*$ becomes a cycle; its only degree-one basis vector is $x_1^*$ with zero differential, so the class is not a boundary and $F_{-1}\ne0$. The $G_{-1}$ source has only $x_0^*$ in degree zero, and its differential $Ux_1^*$ is retained; $Ux_2^*$ lies above $j=-1$ and is excluded. Hence $G_{-1}=0$ and the exact epsilon convention gives $-1$. The degree-zero chain space has basis $x_0^*,Ux_2^*$; their individual differentials are both $Ux_1^*$, so the only nonzero cycle is $x_0^*+Ux_2^*$, and it represents the normalized generator. ## Statement

Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots, and use the epsilon sign convention from the preceding definition. If their knot Floer complexes are stably filtered equivalent, meaning that there are totally acyclic bifiltered complexes $A$ and $B$ with $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A$ filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(J)\oplus B$, then $\epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)$. The acyclic summands here need not be acyclic after taking either associated-graded filtration.

The invariant satisfies $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$, $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$, and the tensor rules
$$ \epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(K),\qquad \epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\epsilon(K\#J)=\epsilon(J). $$
The converse of $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$ fails: the knot $T_{2,5}\#-T_{4,5}\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ has $\tau=0$ and $\epsilon=1$, where $T_{p,q}$ is the positive $(p,q)$ torus knot and $T_{2,3;2,5}$ is the $(2,5)$ cable of the right-handed trefoil with longitudinal winding two. Epsilon is not an integer-valued homomorphism on the smooth concordance group: the right-handed trefoil has $\epsilon=1$ and its connected sum with itself also has $\epsilon=1$, not $2$.

## Statement

Let $C^-(K)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by $U^n x_r$ for $n\ge0$, with $M(U^n x_r)=M(x_r)-2n$ and $A(U^n x_r)=A(x_r)-n$, and assume $H_*(C^-(K))\cong\mathbb F_2[U]$ with generator in Maslov degree zero. For each integer $s$, let $\mathcal A(K,s)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by those terms $U^n x_r$ with $n\ge0$ and $A(x_r)-n\le s$. For any Maslov-graded $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex $D$, let $\delta(D)$ be the maximal Maslov grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D)$, with $\delta(D)=-\infty$ if no such class exists. Define $\nu^-(K)$ to be the least integer $s$ for which $\delta(\mathcal A(K,s))=0$. Then
$$ 0\le \nu^-(K)\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K), $$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth compact connected oriented properly embedded surface in the four-ball bounded by $K$.

Let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(T_{2,3})$ be the right-handed trefoil staircase on generators $x_0,x_1,x_2$ with $(M,A)(x_0)=(0,1)$, $(M,A)(x_1)=(-1,0)$, $(M,A)(x_2)=(-2,-1)$ and differential $\partial x_1=Ux_0+x_2$, $\partial x_0=\partial x_2=0$. The claim that $\Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(1)$ is obtained by minimizing $F_1(x)$ over the individual displayed basis terms $x_0,x_1,x_2$, instead of over Maslov-zero cycles representing the normalized generator, is false. actual_interface.Statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.
Given: **Given:** The oriented knot, its minimum-genus Seifert surface, the grid and the analytic diagrams in the Statement. All polynomial variables remain independent until a quotient is explicitly taken.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with finite balanced Heegaard data satisfying the strict strong-admissibility condition normalized at all $w$-marks for each specified Spin-c sector. For every positive-rank triangle piece first choose an arbitrarily small pointed Hamiltonian representative with no common intersection of three attaching families, following the pair generators and transporting the actual Spin-c label and strict admissibility. On that representative choose the divisor-compatible nearly symmetric regular end paths and generic source-dependent almost-complex perturbations used for the full-marked triangle counts; at rank zero use the empty-product point model. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For an elementary triangle piece with four-dimensional cobordism $W_r$ represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s|_{W_r},\\ n_{w_i}(\phi),n_{z_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \text{for every marked point}}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)}V^{\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class on $W_r$, and all marked multiplicities in the sum are nonnegative. The restriction $\mathfrak s|_{W_r}$ is taken under the identification of this elementary cobordism with its Kirby piece. The other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.
Given: **Given:** The decorated knot cobordism $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$, fixed $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$, chosen decomposition and auxiliary data of the Definition, with its stated Countable Choice assumptions.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism between doubly pointed knots in $S^3$, and let $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. The representative maps from any two parametrized Kirby decompositions and admissible regular Heegaard choices are filtered $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-equivariantly chain homotopic. $$
\widetilde F_{W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2,\mathfrak s_2}\circ \widetilde F_{W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1,\mathfrak s_1} \simeq \sum_{\substack{\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)\\ \mathfrak s|_{W_i}=\mathfrak s_i,\ i=1,2}} \widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s}.
$$
The sum is over Spin-c structures on the glued cobordism restricting to the specified structures on the two pieces. For $W=S^3\times[0,1]$, $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$ has one element; the sum has one term if the specified structures on the pieces are its restrictions, and is empty otherwise. In the compatible case the composition law is ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. If the restrictions on $Y_{\mathrm{mid}}$ differ, the sector maps are not composable; the formula makes no assertion for that pair.
